quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: Number one, shout out to Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey and B.J. Echols. Boys were balling. Joel Embiid in particular, to have the season that he's had, pretty much playing in 20, 25% of the games, and pretty much be counted out by everyone and to come back and play a series like that, down the stretch, those last three wins that they needed to pick up, he was excellent in all three of them. And everyone else fell in line. Tyrese Maxey continued to play great. B.J. Echols seemed to, you know, I spoke earlier in the series about when Joel comes back, how it really affects B.J. Echols and it really affects him because all of a sudden he turns into the third or fourth option on a team. As I've always tried to tell you all, adjusting from a second option to a fourth option or a third option to a fourth, it drastically changes everything. It changes how many plays you get, how many shots you get, the spots you get your ball in. It changes everything. And so I've always felt like when Joel comes back, it affects B.J. Echols the most.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green highlights the often-overlooked impact of a star player's return on a young player's role, emphasizing how drastically it alters their offensive opportunities and overall game.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: I was a bit surprised by this starting lineup because I think it's a Game 7, I think you got to go all out. For me, my starters would have been Payton Pritchard, Derrick White, Jaylen Brown, Neemias Queta, and Sam Hauser. All five of these guys have experience in these type of situations. You essentially threw three guys out there that had zero experience in these situations. They aborted the mission really fast, but I just don't think you want to set that tone in a Game 7. You want to come out with your heavy hitters. There is no tomorrow. But I think you got to go with your heavy hitters. Obviously, J.T. was a late scratch. But I just don't know how you roll a starting lineup out there, it just sets a tone for the entire game. And although the game ended up close, and they seemingly recovered, those possessions matter in the first quarter. You essentially just rolled it out there, you didn't get these guys much of a chance to be successful. They're going into a Game 7, all of a sudden they're starting, they haven't started many games in their career, now they're starting a Game 7 versus a Philly team that throughout this series has gotten hot, has gotten more confident, and more importantly, has gotten healthy. And I'm just not sure that going this route, I mean, Queta ends up playing 33 minutes and has 17 points and 12 rebounds. Sam Hauser ends up doing what he does, he has 11 points, four for seven from the field, three for six from the three. He ends up doing what he does in 30 minutes. I just don't know the guys that they rolled out there in starting five is the starting five that you want to roll out with in an important game like that.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green strongly criticizes the Celtics' Game 7 starting lineup, arguing that fielding inexperienced players in a do-or-die situation sets a negative tone and doesn't maximize the team's chances, even if some of those players performed well later.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: Joel Embiid, 34 points, 12 rebounds, six assists. And I know a lot of people are saying like, yo, is this a legacy game for Joel Embiid? And I say no, hell no. Joel Embiid is just a great player. Joel Embiid is an NBA MVP. Joel Embiid is all of those things. Gold medalist, perennial All-Star, one of the best bigs in this league. Joel Embiid also for those same reasons is the reason that a game in the first round, I don't care if it's Game 7 or Game 2, doesn't matter, because it's still a first-round game. And we've seen Joel Embiid in the first round. In order for Joel Embiid to have legacy games, Joel Embiid has to get to the Conference Finals. And then Joel Embiid needs to help push that team to the NBA Finals. I don't think if you spoke to Joel Embiid, he would say, oh man, that game I had in Round 1 this year versus Boston is a legacy game. You feel good about it. You feel great about it, you're moving on, right? All of those things. But the job's not done. If Philly goes out here and loses this series, no one's coming around this summer like, yeah, but Joel Embiid played a legacy game in that first-round series. No one's talking about that. The talk is going to be Joel Embiid can't win again. Philly need to break the team up. Joel's going to never be healthy. That's what the talk's going to be. So I hate when people try to set guys up like, oh man, it's a legacy game for Joel Embiid, only to set him up to try to tear him down in the weeks to come. There's no way a guy of Joel Embiid's stature can have a legacy game in the first round when he's still hasn't accomplished ultimately what he wants to accomplish. That is the Conference Finals, that is the NBA Finals, and ultimately trying to win an NBA championship. You can't have a legacy game in the first round when you're trying to accomplish those things, especially and you haven't done it before.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green dismisses the idea of a "legacy game" in the first round for a player of Embiid's caliber, arguing that true legacy-defining performances occur in later playoff stages, and labeling early-round games as such is often a setup for future criticism.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: Jaylen Brown went on his stream yesterday and called out Joel Embiid. Said flopping has ruined our league. Joel Embiid is one of the greatest players that has played basketball, but he flops and he knows it too. And I thought that was interesting because Joel definitely will embellish some calls a bit, and Joel will play the get foul game a bit. And ultimately, I think earlier in Joel's career, it's some of the reason why he struggled during the playoffs and his team struggled because normally, they don't call any of that stuff in the playoffs. I've been watching the playoffs this year pretty intensely and I will say more things, and it's a game-to-game thing, right? You watch some of these other games and there's ticky-tack fouls called. So I'm accustomed to the playoffs where you don't get much call at all. And if you're embellishing a foul, you're trying to get a call, they usually don't call it. You fall down trying to get the call, it's a five-on-four break going the other way. That's usually how the playoffs are refereed. It's been a little different this year, I must say. However, as you all know, not a huge fan of calling a guy once you lost. I just don't love that because it comes off as excuse-making. When you in fact could be telling the dead honest truth. But because you lost, people are always going to say, there's the excuse and they're going to make out what you're saying to be an excuse. So it ultimately doesn't hold weight and I feel like you end up wasting one of your bullets because it doesn't hold weight anyway, because you lost and people just charge it to, oh man, he only saying that because he lost. Would he have said that if he won? Honestly, you don't know the answer because he didn't win. And so I'm always very skeptical about saying things like this after a loss, just because people take it and they do what they want to do with the statement, make it out to be what they want to be. And I'm not too fond of that.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green critiques Jaylen Brown's decision to call out Joel Embiid for flopping after a playoff loss, arguing that such comments are often perceived as excuses and lose credibility, despite potentially being truthful.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: Big question is what's next for this Boston team? Is it the end of the Jaylen Brown, Jayson Tatum era? And I would say no. I don't think it's the end of their era because look at the success they had this year with Jayson Tatum out most of the year, and then Jayson Tatum coming back and them having success. Ultimately getting ahead to a 3-1 lead, obviously they squandered the lead away. But you got right where you want to be. Jayson Tatum unfortunately not able to play in Game 7, and I think that's more of a bigger concern than them squandering away a 3-1 lead. Jayson Tatum's knee out of nowhere, it's hurting. Can't go in Game 7. Surprise, this is a guy who plays all the games by the way. For him to sit out Game 7 was really worrisome to me because I'm like, man, it must be something more. I saw even he mentioned, he said, yeah, one of my legs is still way smaller than the other one. So I get to focus on that this summer if there's a silver lining. But the bigger concern for me is, did Jayson Tatum do something more to that knee? Because you definitely overcompensate coming back from an Achilles injury. That's just the natural course. So I wonder, is the knee issue due to him overcompensating and it finally just caught up with him? He obviously came back playing at a very, very high level, at a very high pace, and jumped right into the fire. That worries me a bit. I do not think this is the end of their era. They still shown what they can compete. I do think they're going to have to improve the team around them. Ultimately the collapse that you saw, yes, Jayson Tatum went out. But I think when you look at the Celtics roster, it's not the best roster. And you can't expect it to be the best roster. Jrue Holiday's not there. Porzingis isn't there. Al Horford isn't there. When you start losing that amount of guys, and you start filling the roster in with the Luke Garzas of the world, with the Ron Harper Juniors of the world, Bailey Shermans all getting playing time now, it changes everything. And so I think, keeping those guys, they're going to have to take a deep look at their roster. How do they improve? I know they were able to get under the tax to ultimately build back for this year. All right, so how do you improve the team now? That's what I think is most important. How do you build around Jayson and Jaylen? I think will be the biggest focus and biggest question mark around the Boston Celtics.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green expresses concern over Jayson Tatum's mysterious Game 7 absence, suggesting it might be a more significant injury than acknowledged, and questions how the Celtics will improve their roster around their stars after shedding salary.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: Pistons beat the Magic 116 to 94 to advance to the second round and face the Cavs after being down 3-1 in the series. Now, my worry with this series is the same worry that I have with the next series or last series, which is coming back from down 3-1. Did you ultimately expend too much energy to get through those first-round series having to fight back from 3-1 deficits? That is going to be the question for the Pistons. That is also a big question for who we just spoke about, the Philadelphia 76ers. I know when you come off emotional wins like that, A, Game 1 is usually tough. So if I'm the Cleveland Cavaliers, if I am the Philadelphia 76ers, obviously Cleveland had a seven-game series as well, but you're going on the road and you have a free swing. So, let me tell you how this goes. Both of these teams have had one day to implement a playoff game plan. I'll just be straightforward with you, it won't be the most thorough playoff game plan. It's just impossible to think that guys can grasp that much in a day. It's not a realistic thing in the NBA. To think that coaches have enough time to install everything that they need to install, it's too quick. And so that quick one-day turnaround ultimately can work to the benefit of the away team. Because you're coming in with a free swing. Our game plan isn't always set the way it's going to be throughout this series. But we got a free swing. We're supposed to lose this game. We're on one day rest, coming off of a Game 7. We should lose. Let's go in, let's take a free swing. That has to be the mindset of the Cavs. That has to be the mindset of the Philadelphia 76ers. That must be the mindset because you don't often get free swings in an NBA playoff series. In this Game 1, you have a completely free swing at the Detroit Pistons. You have a completely free swing at the New York Knicks if you're Philly. And I think you really got to come in, try and take advantage of them, right? You really got to do that. Because just like also, just like yourself, these teams have had one day to prepare. They could have prepared for two games, two different teams, you know, citing one of the other wins. But you still got one game to prepare. So I think this is both of those teams' chance to come in and steal a Game 1, which completely shifts the series right away if they're able to do that.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green questions whether teams coming off a 3-1 playoff comeback will have enough energy for the next series, suggesting that their opponents should exploit the quick turnaround and emotional fatigue by treating Game 1 as a "free swing."

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: Cade Cunningham and Tobias Harris put the Detroit Pistons on their backs. Cade Cunningham 32 and 12, Tobias Harris 30 and 9. I think, man, Tobias on 61% shooting. Tobias stepped up in every way in that series from veteran leadership, to making big buckets when they needed to, to being the second scorer for those guys, to being that steady force throughout that entire series. Tobias stepped up. Coach J.B. Bickerstaff said after the game, nobody can say shit to me about Tobias Harris. Now what I warn Coach J.B. of is, it's a first-round series player and y'all are the number one seed. Going to need Jalen Duren to play better. But Tobias stepped up in Jalen Duren's absence if you will. Now, you still got to go do it again because again, y'all were down 3-1, make no mistake about it. But you're not supposed to be down 3-1 in the first round as the number one seed. So it's a hole that they dug themselves and they had to dig themselves out of it. Kudos to the Detroit Pistons that they did dig themselves out of it. However, we can't just completely stamp guys after a Round 1 series. Did what he's supposed to do, no question. Love how he was the steady force, but now you got to go do it again because you're supposed to win the second-round series. Right? So I need guys to go improve this to me second round, Conference Finals, Finals. When you're the number one seed, the expectations rise. This was last year, I'll roll with you on that one J.B. You guys are the number one seed, I can't necessarily roll with that in the first round of playoffs and being the number one seed. Tip my hat to the guys though, they stepped up. But in order to win this next series, Jalen Duren is going to have to play better. They will not continue to get through the playoffs and their better players aren't playing good. That's just not how this works. He's going to have to play better. Now, we'll get into the keys of the next series later, but kudos to the Pistons, way to battle back. And in turn, they battled back. Orlando Magic, third consecutive first-round playoff exit. And this morning, of course, Coach Jamal Mosley gets fired. And you have to ask yourself the question, what's next with this Orlando team? You got Jalen Suggs making a boatload of money. A lot of people didn't feel like he played up to par. At some point going into Game 7, he had missed 31 of his last 39 shots. What do you do with Jalen Suggs? Is he back next year? Can you even trade that contract if you wanted to? What happens with that? A lot of people have thought over time that they needed to move on from either and choose between Franz or Paolo. And watching this playoff series before Franz went down, it didn't look like they needed to choose between those two guys. Now, things change when you lose, people see things differently. But I don't know that the answer is getting rid of one of those two guys with the way they played down the stretch. I think ultimately they're going to have to try to find better offensive consistency, offensive flow. But man, Paolo showed y'all who he was. I've been raving about Paolo on this podcast since Paolo was at Duke. Did he come out and show y'all who the fuck he is? Yes, he did. He did all that he could to carry that team through. And he was frustrated as hell in that press conference afterwards, and I agree with him. Love how he didn't sugarcoat his answer. I want to say, we're good enough, but we've lost in the first round each of the last three seasons. So in saying that, no, the results will say we're not. But I want to believe that we are. Results will say we are. I tip my hat to Paolo. Kudos to him. That's how you handle it. You don't run from it. Run straight to it. We lost, we fell short. Acknowledge it, head on. Now what are you going to do about it this summer? So, I found that very interesting. It'll be interesting to see if they feel that they need to move on from one of those two guys. I know they're very happy with the Desmond Bane trade. What happens with Jalen Suggs? Wendell Carter had been on the block before, comes out and completely stifles Jalen Duren, who's an All-Star center. Not sure you want to get off him at this point. Who's the next coach up? We've heard rumors about Tom Thibodeau. Is he the best fit for these guys? I think, one thing we know that Coach Thibs is great, and brings a winning culture to any team that he goes to. Is he the coach for this group? Every team he's gone to has gotten better. Is it, for a team that needs and lacks offensive creativity? I love Coach Thibs. I think he's going to need to bring in an offensive mastermind with him and delegate some of that to make this roster fit together if he was to take this Orlando job. So, it'll be interesting to see what happens here. But, overall, tip my hat to Cade Cunningham, not fold under the pressure. Tip my hat to Tobias Harris. I also tip my cap to Isaiah Stewart. Isaiah Stewart was a dominant force in that series. Defensively, protecting the rim, bringing a level of physicality that you got to bring to the game when you're down 3-1 if you're going to have a chance to come back. I tip my hat to Isaiah Stewart. Just getting it done by any means necessary. Being that force, you see the young fella struggling. Saw a good young fella, I got you. Watch this. Tip my hat to Isaiah Stewart. He was the X, obviously Tobias did what Tobias needed to do. But the X-factor in that series for the Pistons was Isaiah Stewart. So I tip my cap to him.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green praises Tobias Harris and Cade Cunningham for leading the Pistons' 3-1 comeback but warns that Jalen Duren needs to step up in the next round. He also discusses the Magic's future after firing their coach, questioning roster decisions and potential coaching changes.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: Cavs beat the Raptors 114 to 102 to advance to the second round and face the Pistons. Jarrett Allen finally stepped up and had a huge game with 22 points, 19 rebounds, and three blocks. I guess he got over his fear of the lights being too bright. Started yelling at R.J. Barrett in the final seconds, go home, go home. I love to see guys on that type of time. And when you step up and have a game like that, Jarrett Allen, you can talk like that. You can show up like that. Problem is, Jarrett Allen, we've seen you can do it. We've seen the lights dim for you a bit. Can you keep that going in the second round? Because guess what, them lights get brighter and brighter as teams drop off. It's less teams now. It is eight teams left in the NBA playoffs, not 16. Can you do that again? So I think that's one of the keys for the Cavs. When James first got traded to the Cavaliers, it unlocked Jarrett Allen. And then he kind of went back down again. James said yesterday, when he's playing with that type of force, we're a completely different team. And it's true. You're going to need him or Evan Mobley to play at that level. That hasn't quite been the case with this ball club of getting both of those guys playing at an extremely high level together. So, you're going to need the same Jarrett Allen. Obviously, it won't be 22 and 19 every night, but the force he played with, how he was going to get them offensive rebounds. He just looked like he wanted the ball and he wanted it more than anyone else. So, the excuse of the lights being too bright doesn't work anymore. You got to use this and you got to build on that. You've overcome that now. And it was great to see him come out of that shell, play a great game, and ultimately, lead the Cleveland Cavaliers to the second round of the playoffs. Because I think without his performance, there's no way that they get to the second round of the playoffs. So, tip my hat to Jarrett Allen, but unfortunately, it's just the first round, big fella, and you're going to have to do it again.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green praises Jarrett Allen's breakout Game 7 performance, challenging him to maintain that intensity as the playoff lights get brighter, noting that his consistent force is crucial for the Cavaliers' success.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: Scottie Barnes had an incredible series averaging 24, nine rebounds, and six assists on 51% shooting. A lot of people compare his defense to mine, which I take as an honor. But I told you all before, I think Scottie Barnes is an incredible defender. The way he cover up mistakes for people, with his size and length and the way he can move, he can legitimately guard positions one through five. And I think he showed that in this series. And it was beautiful to watch. Now, I think the question's been answered, can you build around Scottie Barnes? Now they really have to go take a look at this roster. Is Jakob Poeltl best around Scottie Barnes? Or do you need to look at Scottie Barnes more like a Giannis? Do he need a shooting five as opposed to Jakob Poeltl clogging the paint up? So I think that's something to look at. Immanuel Quickley's on a large salary. How does he fit with this team? How does he make this team better? Ultimately questions that you have to answer. I know my goal moving forward would be, I need to put the best guys I can around Scottie Barnes. And when I do that, we're going to give ourselves a chance to get back in contention. Scottie Barnes did what he did this series, missing Brandon Ingram I think the last three games, and also B.I. didn't have his best series, and Scottie Barnes continued to play. So, with Brandon Ingram being ruled out, I think ultimately it definitely impacted the game because it's just another guy that you don't have to account for. I think Brandon Ingram is the one guy on their team that can just go get it for himself at any time, any way. And so I think it definitely impacted the outcome, but overall, tip my hat to Scottie Barnes.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green praises Scottie Barnes' versatile defense and questions the Raptors' roster construction around him, particularly the fit of Jakob Poeltl and Immanuel Quickley's large contract, suggesting they need to optimize the team to maximize Barnes' potential.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: Now we will move into these Conference Semifinals matchups and that is the 76ers versus the Knicks. They split the season series two to two. Knicks come in rested with their last game being Thursday. Ultimately, you always wonder, is it rest versus rust? And quite honestly, they played Thursday, playing again on Monday. That's not enough time to get rusty. It is enough time to get rested. And so I think that ultimately bodes well for the New York Knicks. Now, coming into this series, you got to look at what matchups are going to be key in this series. Obviously, you got Embiid versus Kat. They'll have to guard each other, unless you do something funky with the matchups. But more than likely, they're going to have to guard each other. Kat is a tough matchup for Embiid because he's going to pull him out away from the rim. You got to be up on that trail three. So with that being said, I'm not sure I'm putting Embiid on Kat. You may have to throw Paul George on him to start the game. Because him pulling Embiid out, like you need Embiid healthy to have a chance to win this series. And him pulling Embiid out away from the basket, it just creates more torque on the body, creates more movement on his knees, puts him in a vulnerable situation, I think, having him chasing around Kat on out on the open court. And so I don't know that that's a great matchup. When I look at that matchup, it's going to be very vital in this series. However, Kat can't guard Embiid either. Cannot guard him. Do you throw O.G. Anunoby on Embiid? But then who do you put Kat on if you do that? So, it's going to be interesting to see which way Mike Brown and Nick Nurse go with these matchups. Because I think it's going to play a heavy, heavy, heavy role in the outcome of this series.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green breaks down the critical Embiid vs. Towns matchup, highlighting Towns' ability to pull Embiid away from the rim and the physical toll it could take on Embiid, while also questioning who else could effectively guard either star.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: And as I promised before we get out of here, needed to touch on some people talking or a person talking in particular. Saw what Kenny Smith and Stephen A. said and, the interesting thing about, and Stephen A. hinted at it. The interesting thing about my comments last week about Coach Kerr's article in the New Yorker and what I shared. The interesting thing about it is, it's about three minutes of me praising my coach, of me saying how I wouldn't be who I am without my coach, of me speaking on the things that my coach have done for me. Of me sharing why I and we had the success that we've had. And then there's like maybe 15 seconds where I spoke about hindering my offense. And now, I don't like to get in these back and forth because quite honestly, the guys that you usually get into the back and forth with, they become back and forth because there's like a weight that's like one of them like severely tips something this way and the other one just like kind of so far down that it kind of pulls you back a little bit. And so, speaking of Austin Rivers, I saw he said he's bewildered and it's ridiculous or what I said. And I just find it interesting that a guy who was the 10th pick in my draft, I was 35, who's on his second act, I'm still on Act 1, would say such things. He goes, Draymond, it's never been a scorer. Well, Austin, you and I average the same amount of points in high school when you were a scorer. So I don't know what would qualify Austin Rivers to speak about scoring when in high school, me and you average the same amount of points. And I say high school because that's when you were at your best. That's when Austin Rivers was Austin Rivers in high school. And so that's why I point out the high school scoring because, I want to make it fair. I want to speak about him when he was at his best. And he was at his best at Winter Park, if I remember correctly. He had ESPN games, like that's when he was at his best. When he was faster than everybody and could just put his head down and drive right and get to the rim. And then in college, he was still good. He was very featured at Duke and had a very big moment, where he hit the three on the wing, like, you got to give him credit. That's when he was at his best. In college, he averaged almost 17 points a game in the Big 10. Very limited possessions. So I only want to speak about Austin at his best. Because NBA careers, should he really talk about my NBA career? I don't know that that's the case. I'm still with my first team. He was gone from his first team in two years. And so I just like, sometimes you just should not say something. Always isn't the time to everything isn't something you should speak on. And I don't think that was really one for Austin Rivers to be bewildered about and like say it's ridiculous. Because like, the guy received the biggest bailout in U.S. history prior to President Trump, the airlines, when they needed it. Austin Rivers received the biggest bailout in NBA history. Excuse me, in world history, in U.S. history. Received the biggest bailout in U.S. history when his dad gave him $42 million. And I tip my hat to Doc. I pray that one day, I mean, it won't be $42 million then because NBA is going up so much. But I pray that I can give D.J. $200 million or give Deuce $250 million. I pray that I can do that one day. So I tip my hat to Doc, in his incredible bailout of his son and putting good money in his pocket, man. I really tip my hat to him. But, if you, if you listen to the whole thing, the whole three minutes of what I spoke about, what a competent basketball mind would have heard was, man, this guy who wanted to do this, who thought he was this, changed his game and then still became this because that's what worked best for the team. Never shared those gripes because they didn't matter. And by the way, still don't matter. Because guess what? I don't care. I'm totally fine. My career's been great. So I found it interesting for people who need things to speak on to make it out as if I'm sitting here complaining about my career has been so bad. No, my career has been great. Possibly Hall of Fame worthy. I got nothing to sit and complain about. But if you go listen to the context of what I said, I said all of these great things about the coach that's helped me incredibly, incredibly large amount. Who I said, man, not sure where I'd be if he wasn't my coach. And I love how people just go take the 15 seconds that they want to take and make it a headline. But I really enjoyed watching Austin Rivers be bewildered by a statement of a guy who was drafted after him, still doing it after he's done, long after he's done, at a higher level right now today than he ever did it. Right now today, more impactful. Bar none. Now, had Austin Rivers taken a page out of my book and said, man, these people really don't need me to score, let me go do something else. Probably doesn't need the bailout. Because then you go defend, you go be the backup point guard than what he ultimately was. Like you carve out a nice niche for yourself. So what I can't teach you about is carving out a niche for yourself since you're bewildered about my comments. I could have taught him to be carve out a niche as I did. So what you should go show kids is, man, here's a guy who was the national player of the year in college, was a big 10 player of the year, that got to the league actually because he could score in all these different ways. He could shoot the three, he could get off the dribble, he could take you to the block. That's how he got to the league. And showing at times that he could score in the league, but that just wasn't the path. So look, he went and did this. But by the way, to act as if, and here was my problem with Kenny, Kenny Smith, that's not a problem, but for all the people out there, to act, you can talk to any basketball player in the world. They're going to have a gripe about their coach, some gripe. All things could be great. They're going to say one thing negative about the coach. Not negative, but just like something that they feel could be better for them. That's every player in the world. You go ask LeBron James about each coach he's played for. I guarantee you he has some gripe about that coach when he played for. That's basketball. That's what we're in. There's going to be a gripe. Every player, you go talk to Steph Curry right now, who's never had a bad, negative thing to say about Steve. And if you talk to him, I guarantee you he's going to have some gripe. Because that's every basketball player in the world. If you talk to Coach Kerr about playing for Phil Jackson, about playing for Coach, he's going to have some gripe. That is basketball. So I was I'm a little bewildered that I can say all of these great things. And the one thing that I say that was my small gripe, it's like, oh my God, it's world news. Thankful for the voice that moves the landscape. Great. I appreciate that. But when you get guys like Austin Rivers, who again, received the biggest bailout in U.S. history, to say something like that, I was bewildered. I'm still bewildered because, man, you just got to know like, sometimes it ain't, and I may feel this way, but sometimes I may not be the right person to say this. And so, I think it's best that, you know, you you had more the the voice would have been loud, was louder when you was arguing with the one-on-one guys, not Nas. The voice, you know, we heard your voice more then because again, we get it. You know, you you possibly can speak a little bit more to that. So, you know, you got these guys calling you out and you don't want to go play against them and all like, you should focus on that more and the 24-hour fitness runs that you want to go get your shit off in. Like those are like you should come and speak about those because you accomplished enough to be able to speak about those. Unfortunately, you didn't accomplish enough to to like to do that. It's crazy. I was shocked. So, I wish him well in this one-on-one matchup if he decided to take on that challenge. I hope he don't take on that challenge because I've been I I've watched some of that one-on-one stuff. And if he's smart, don't go play Nas. He's going to body him like crazy. So, don't go play him. But stay in your lane.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green delivers a scathing response to Austin Rivers' criticism, highlighting Rivers' "bailout" contract from his father and contrasting their NBA careers, arguing that Rivers lacks the credibility to comment on Draymond's game or coaching relationship.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.quote: Ultimately, listen, Pistons are supposed to win this series. They don't have the experience that James Harden has in the playoffs. They don't have the experience that Donovan Mitchell has in the playoffs. However, getting over the hump of that first series, I think was huge. And it reminded me of our series versus the Grizzlies in 2015 before we won our first championship. You had a very inexperienced myself, Klay, Steph, we had been in the playoffs two years prior. Lost in the second round, lost in the first round. You got Z-Bo who's been in the Conference Finals, Marc Gasol, Mike Conley, all these guys like they've been joined for a while now. We had to overcome a 2-1 deficit. That's what the Pistons just went through reminds me of. And you band together off that. And I think these Pistons are going to band together off that. I think they'll come out, they'll have a great series. And ultimately, I'm taking the Pistons in six.
quotes.why_it_matters: Draymond Green predicts the Pistons will win their second-round series, drawing parallels to his own Warriors team's growth after overcoming an early playoff hurdle, suggesting the Pistons' recent comeback will forge a strong team bond.
